kept.title: Unauthenticated SSRF via DNS Rebinding Mitigation Bypass
kept.description: The logic in `is_hostname_resolve_to_internal_ip` (helpers.ts:310) attempts to prevent DNS rebinding by performing two resolutions and comparing results, but it uses a flawed delay-based strategy and does not fully sanitize inputs, allowing attackers to exploit race conditions between resolution and final URL usage.
steps_to_exploit: Register a malicious domain
Point it to an external public IP initially
Trigger the check which sees the external IP
Update the domain record to point to 127.0.0.1 immediately after the first check completes
The subsequent HTTP request by the application will target the internal IP
kept.impact: Attackers can bypass security controls to access internal network resources, services, or metadata APIs.

kept.title: Use of 'got' Dependency without Agent/Proxy Pinning
kept.description: The `is_redirect_safe` function (helpers.ts:460) uses the `got` library to perform HEAD requests for validation. Without a custom agent that explicitly restricts connections to internal IPs, the `got` library will follow redirects or resolve addresses that are not properly blocked at the transport layer.
steps_to_exploit: Supply a URL that performs an HTTP 302 redirect
Redirect the URL to an internal IP address (e.g., http://169.254.169.254/)
The `got` client will follow the redirect to the forbidden internal resource bypassing the initial validation
kept.impact: Full SSRF bypass enabling internal network scanning and data exfiltration.

kept.title: Incomplete Blacklist for Internal IP Ranges
kept.description: The `BAD_RANGE_USED_IN_SSRF` list in `src/helpers.ts` (lines 21-36) is hardcoded and incomplete, failing to include specific IPv6 unique local addresses or other obscure reserved segments that are reachable in cloud environments.
steps_to_exploit: Identify an internal service or cloud metadata IP not present in the manual list
Use the application's URL validation functions to reach the forbidden host
Application will classify the IP as safe and allow the request
kept.impact: Bypass of SSRF protection for non-standard internal addresses.

kept.title: Dangerous use of require() for 'got' dependency
kept.description: The `src/helpers.ts` file uses `require("got").default` (line 6), which is brittle in an ESM-heavy environment and can lead to unexpected module loading behaviors or prototype pollution if dependencies are improperly resolved.
steps_to_exploit: Perform a dependency confusion attack if the environment is misconfigured
Inject a malicious 'got' module
Execution of arbitrary code during the validation logic
kept.impact: Remote code execution in the context of the application server.

kept.title: Insufficient Unicode Normalization Logic
kept.description: The `normalize_unicode` function uses NFKC (src/helpers.ts:496). While helpful, it does not address bypasses related to Homograph attacks or non-standard Unicode variations that could confuse DNS resolution or internal proxy logic.
steps_to_exploit: Use a domain name containing visually similar Unicode characters (homoglyphs)
Bypass blacklist filters that rely on string matching rather than canonicalized representations
kept.impact: Allows attackers to bypass domain-based blacklists and masking filters.

kept.title: Use of 'ts-ignore' for internal security checks
kept.description: The `is_ip_internal` function contains several `@ts-ignore` comments (src/helpers.ts:240, 259) to suppress type checking on IP parsing and matching. This masks potential runtime errors where types mismatch, leading to bypasses in logic evaluation.
steps_to_exploit: Pass specially crafted malformed IP structures that break logic when forced as strings
Observe where the code bypasses checks because the comparison logic fails due to type mismatches
kept.impact: Security logic failures causing the library to incorrectly validate malicious URLs as safe.

kept.title: Insecure Timing for DNS Resolution
kept.description: The implementation of `resolveWithDelay` (src/helpers.ts:320) uses `setTimeout` with very short, randomized delays. These are insufficient to prevent fast-flux DNS rebinding attacks where the TTL is set to zero.
steps_to_exploit: Configure DNS TTL to 0 for a domain
Swap the IP address during the ~200ms delay window
The check will return inconsistent results that fail to block the request
kept.impact: Successful DNS rebinding leading to SSRF.

kept.title: Over-reliance on 'URL' constructor for parsing
kept.description: The `is_url_safe` function (src/helpers.ts:503) relies on the `URL` constructor. The behavior of `new URL()` varies across Node.js versions, and it may not properly parse edge-case URL formats that might be interpreted differently by the underlying request library (`got`).
steps_to_exploit: Pass a URL with non-standard syntax (e.g., encoded backslashes or multiple fragments)
The parser might misidentify the hostname, while the final request client resolves it to the correct internal address
kept.impact: SSRF vulnerability due to parsing discrepancy.

kept.title: Lack of Input Sanitization for 'is_ipv6'
kept.description: The `is_ipv6` function (src/helpers.ts:12) uses `ipaddr.IPv6.isValid(ip)`. This function is highly sensitive to input format; if passed non-string types or malformed objects, it may crash or behave unexpectedly (handled via generic try-catch returning false).
steps_to_exploit: Pass non-string objects to trigger the catch block
If used in a critical path, bypasses may occur due to incorrect handling of type casting
kept.impact: Potential security bypasses if IPv6 addresses are misclassified.

kept.title: Unsafe Regex in `normalize_ipv4`
kept.description: The regex `^\d{1,3}(\.\d{1,3}){3}$` (src/helpers.ts:196) does not check the bounds of the octets before parsing, relying on manual checks that might be skipped if the logic flow is manipulated.
steps_to_exploit: Inject long numeric strings that overflow or cause unexpected parsing behavior before the octet range check occurs
kept.impact: Incorrect normalization of IP addresses leading to potential blacklist bypasses.

kept.title: Use of 'process.env.DSSRF_MAKE_REQUEST'
kept.description: The library reads `process.env.DSSRF_MAKE_REQUEST` (src/helpers.ts:8), which suggests there might be an execution path that performs requests not intended for production usage, potentially leading to unauthorized data exfiltration.
steps_to_exploit: Set the environment variable in a development or production container to enable dangerous features
kept.impact: Exposing unintended functionality that could lead to unauthorized network requests.

kept.title: Excessive reliance on try-catch for security validation
kept.description: Many functions, including `is_url_safe` (src/helpers.ts:503), return `false` on any exception. If an exception occurs, it defaults to blocking, but if the logic is malformed, it could inadvertently permit unsafe paths if logic flow assumes successful parsing occurred.
steps_to_exploit: Pass malformed strings that trigger exceptions in early stages of the validation chain
kept.impact: Denial of service or incorrect security classification of input URLs.

kept.title: Manual string replacement for URL structure
kept.description: Functions like `replace_backslash_with_slash_in_string` (src/helpers.ts:378) modify URL structure before validation. This manual manipulation is a common anti-pattern that deviates from standard URL parsing (RFC 3986), causing discrepancies.
steps_to_exploit: Use backslashes or other non-standard separators that are ignored by some browsers but interpreted differently by `new URL()`
kept.impact: Bypassing filters by masquerading malicious characters as benign URL components.

kept.title: Hardcoded debug logs in exposed functions
kept.description: The function `is_url_safe_debug` (src/helpers.ts:525) logs input parameters, which might include sensitive user-supplied URLs potentially containing tokens, credentials, or PII.
steps_to_exploit: Call the debug function with a URL containing sensitive data
The sensitive data will appear in the application logs or console
kept.impact: Information disclosure of potentially sensitive user input.

kept.title: Insecure default configuration for redirects
kept.description: Redirection checking is disabled by default via `DSSRF_CHECK_REDIRECTS` (helpers.ts:513). Developers may integrate this library assuming it is secure, while failing to set the environment variable, leading to an SSRF vulnerability via redirects.
steps_to_exploit: Integrate the library without setting the environment variable
Perform an SSRF attack through a simple HTTP redirect
kept.impact: SSRF vulnerabilities in applications that rely on this library for URL validation.
